### §5.1 Interfaces and common well-formedness   [ISA-5.1]

````text
ISA-5.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] Signatures list roles: `oracle @o (in a: wire[8]) (tgt t: wire[8]) (fault f: wire[4]) (mem db: region[10,8] in) (args n: i64)`.
  <1>2 [def] **Interface regions** are caller-owned, passed by name, role `in` (returned to entry contents on every basis configuration) or `mut` (actions only).
  <1>3 [req] In the text form (§16.2) a wire param's role suffix is optional and, when present, MUST equal its group's role (`in` in an oracle's or action's `in` group, `mut` in an action's `mut` group); a region param always carries its role (`in` or `mut`); other region-interface params carry no suffix.   deps: ISA-16.2
  <1>4 [req] Lproc parameter roles are specified in §3.7 and §16.2.   deps: ISA-3.7, ISA-16.2
  <1>5 [req] A region MUST NOT contain `measure effect br call uncall trap hostcall qreg.* budget.mint` or classical memory instructions, nor lifted rows outside oracle bodies.
  <1>6 [req] Predicate stack empty at entry and exit.
  <1>7 [req] Every `qalloc` matched by a `qfree` of a clean bundle, every `qborrow` by a `qreturn` after its frame, every local `qregion` restored, by **explicit cleanup instructions**; the schedule chooses only realisations.   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle)
  <1>8 [req] **`in` wires in actions** appear only as controls (including the address operands of `qload qunload qstore qexchm`, the wires pushed by `qpred`, the selector of `qif`, whose two `x` gates restore it, and the `cond` wires of `qloop … while`), as targets of diagonal gates, as `qcopy`/`qxor` sources, as the value operand of `qstore` (it is only read, as the control of the XOR into the selected cell), or as `in` arguments of calls.
  <1>9 [req] The **region call graph** — an edge from a function to the callee of each of its `oracle_call`, `action_call`, `lift.oracle_call`, `lift.oracle_uncall` and `lift.perm_call` instructions and to both callees of each `qinplace`, an oracle counting the rows of its lproc closure as its own — is acyclic (suite F); recursion exists only through `lift.call` among lprocs.   deps: ISA-3.6-P1.S1 (lproc closure), ISA-2-P4.S1 (lproc)
````

### §5.2 Lifted oracle   [ISA-5.2]

````text
ISA-5.2-P1
  <1>1 [def] **Body**: lifted and control rows over its locations and lproc closure; **exact-permutation only** (ε = 0 everywhere, transitively).   deps: ISA-3.6-P1.S1 (lproc closure)
ISA-5.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Contract** on every x ∈ D: `ins` unchanged; `tgt` final = initial ⊕ payload(F_B(x)); `fr` final = initial ⊕ code(F_B(x)); `in` regions unchanged; borrowed bundles returned (§5.6); workspace, locations, local regions, step state clean / at image.   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle), ISA-5.6
  <1>2 [req] **F_B(x)** = `(f(x), 0)` if the reference interpreter reaches `lift.retval` within B steps without a fault (f(x) = the XOR-accumulated `result_val`), else `(0, code)` with `code` the first fault in sequential order, or `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS` if not halted after B steps.
  <1>3 [req] The oracle is an **involution** on `(ins, tgt, fr)` and its own adjoint.
ISA-5.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Construction**: (1) allocate step state (`result_val` included), locations, local regions, `alloctab` pre-entries, B frames; (2) run B forward steps; (3) **commit**: `at_HALT = (pc == HALT)`; under `at_HALT ∧ ¬faulted`: `qxor result_val tgt`; under `faulted`: `qxor code fr`; under `¬at_HALT`: XOR the constant `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS` into `fr`; uncompute `at_HALT`; (4) **prefix reversal**: run the inverse step for t = B..1, then release (1).
    <2>1 [req] (1) allocate step state (`result_val` included), locations, local regions, `alloctab` pre-entries, B frames
    <2>2 [req] (2) run B forward steps
    <2>3 [req] (3) **commit**: `at_HALT = (pc == HALT)`; under `at_HALT ∧ ¬faulted`: `qxor result_val tgt`; under `faulted`: `qxor code fr`; under `¬at_HALT`: XOR the constant `FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS` into `fr`; uncompute `at_HALT`
    <2>4 [req] (4) **prefix reversal**: run the inverse step for t = B..1, then release (1).
  <1>2 [req] The commit writes persist.
ISA-5.2-P4
  <1>1 [def] **Domain D**: every value of each `ins`, of `tgt`, of `fr`, of every cell of every `in` region, of every borrowed bundle; `qalloc`ed wires at 0; local regions at image.   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle)
````

### §5.3 Quantum action   [ISA-5.3]

````text
ISA-5.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] **Semantics.** The body denotes a unitary U on mut ⊗ ins ⊗ mem_mut ⊗ (borrowed), block-diagonal in the computational basis of `ins` and of `in`-region cells, identity on borrowed and external reference systems (§5.6), workspace returned clean.   deps: ISA-5.6
  <1>2 [req] No fault outcome.
  <1>3 [req] Coherent internal control yields the padded unitary under declared bounds, part of the action's identity.
  <1>4 [def] **Permutation action**: realised unitary a permutation matrix (ε = 0, permutation gates only, transitively).
ISA-5.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Body**: gates; `qcopy quncopy qxor qexch qinplace`; `qload qunload qstore qexchm`; `qpred qunpred qif qloop`; `oracle_call action_call`; `qalloc qborrow qfree qreturn`; `qregion`.
  <1>2 [req] An action body with several `block`s executes its blocks in text order, each a unitary fragment; labels are descriptive and carry no control semantics, and lifetimes may span blocks.
ISA-5.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Bounds.** The `bounds { … }` list of an action's `regs` line and the `bounds` array of its signature hold, in text order, the trip count `n` of every `qloop` and `qloop … while` in the body (nested loops included, outer before inner); the list MUST equal the body (suite F) and is empty for a body without loops.
  <1>2 [req] It is part of the action's identity because the padded unitary of coherent internal control depends on it.
ISA-5.3-P4
  <1>1 [def] **Adjoint table** (reverse order, instruction replaced, versions renumbered):
  <1>2 [def] (code block, 10 lines) rx/ry/rz(θ) ↦ (−θ) s ↔ sdg t ↔ tdg x cx ccx mcx swap h cz: self-adjoint   deps: ISA-4.6
ISA-5.3-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Control.** `ctl w @a` is controlled-U: workspace, regions and flags allocated unconditionally; every gate of the body and its cleanup runs under `w` in addition to the active predicate.
ISA-5.3-P6
  <1>1 [req] The shorthand `qif w {adj A}{adj B}` denotes that adjoint when each arm's allocations and releases are matched within that arm; no arm-local lifetime restriction is imposed on the source `qif`.   declared: ISA-3.5, ISA-4.6-P7, ISA-5.1
ISA-5.3-P7
  <1>1 [req] Two operations form a **matched pair** iff the second is the §5.3 adjoint of the first, with the same callee(s) (the pair exchanged for `qinplace`), identical classical argument values and token identities and tuples, the same operand wires with the first's read-only input versions and produced target versions current at the second, and equal effective control sets including the versions of their wires; order and repetition in predicate stacks are irrelevant.   deps: ~ISA-5.3   declared: ISA-2-P10, ISA-3.3-P3, ISA-4.5-P5, ISA-4.7, ISA-5.3-P4, ISA-5.4
  <1>2 [req] A matched inverse restores preceding wire-version bindings for subsequent matching only when the §6.2 cleanup conditions hold; matching alone does not discharge an outstanding-reader or phase obligation, and a cell write always advances its cell version even when its value is restored.   deps: ISA-6.2   declared: ISA-3.3-P3, ISA-6.1-P1, ISA-6.2
ISA-5.3-P8
  <1>1 [req] Scheduled action adjoints use the source replacements above before reference-recipe instantiation, with the ordinal contract and `adj` adapter specified in §11.1 (K62).   deps: ~ISA-0.2-P62.S1 (K62), ~ISA-11.1   declared: ISA-5.3-P4, ISA-11-P2, ISA-11.1-P29
````

### §5.4 Budgets and fault codes   [ISA-5.4]

````text
ISA-5.4-P1
  <1>1 [unc] Lproc token parameters forward existing tokens; they neither mint a token nor alter its validity or tuple.
  <1>2 [req] Binding and forwarding have no separate budget charge (§3.7); a lifted region call inside an lproc has the same charge and token semantics as in an oracle body.   deps: ISA-2-P4.S1 (lproc), ISA-3.7-P1.S1 (oracle body), ISA-3.7
  <1>3 [req] In particular, the enclosing oracle's token is not implicitly substituted for a nested call's explicit token.
ISA-5.4-P2
  <1>1 [def] Budget = (B, heap_limit, stack_limit, depth_limit), classical.   deps: ISA-2-P5.S1 (Budget)
  <1>2 [req] `bennett_ budget` validates: `heap_limit ≤ layout.heap_limit_max`, `stack_limit ≤ 2^S_cells`, `depth_limit < 2^Dc − 1`; for a memoryless object (§7.2) `heap_limit = stack_limit = depth_limit = 0`.   deps: ISA-7.2
  <1>3 [req] B is enforced by running exactly B steps; heap, stack and depth are wire counters.
  <1>4 [non] *(non-normative, used by §4.5)* If the reference interpreter succeeds on x under a tuple β₀, it succeeds with the same result under every tuple β ≥ β₀ componentwise: its only limit-dependent decisions are the flags of `lift.alloc` and `lift.call`, false on that trajectory and still false with larger limits, and the step bound, not reached.   deps: ISA-4.5
  <1>5 [req] A nested `lift.oracle_call` row uses the tuple of its own token, not β, which is why §4.5 fixes those tuples exactly.   deps: ISA-4.5
ISA-5.4-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Tokens.** A token denotes a validated tuple (B, heap_limit, stack_limit, depth_limit) and the oracle it was validated for; a region call uses the tuple of the token it is given, and a token MAY be supplied to any region call of the program (the checks above depend only on the object's layout).
  <1>2 [req] Tokens come from `bennett_budget` (§10; valid until the program is unloaded) or from **`tk = budget.mint @o s h st d`** (CC and R): `@o` names an oracle of the program (a symbol reference, §9.2) whose object's layout the checks use, and is recorded with the token for diagnostics only; s, h, st, d are `i64` values read as unsigned 64-bit; the instruction applies exactly `bennett_budget`'s checks to (s, h, st, d) before any mutation; failure is a fault record `FAULT_UB_TRAP` (§4.9) and no token; success produces a fresh token for that tuple, valid until its frame is reversed or its run is CLOSED, and never constructible from an integer.   deps: ISA-10, ISA-9.2, ISA-4.9
  <1>3 [req] A region call given a token that is not valid is a CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP` before any effect (a launch argument: `E_ARG`).   deps: ISA-4.9-P1.S1 (CC trap)
  <1>4 [req] A minted tuple binds its invocation exactly as a host-minted one does (§11, §12): an invocation whose closure hash, variant, inherited controls, tuple and `params_hash` equal the `bindings` of the object's schedule executes that schedule; any other invocation executes under the §11 defaults; a consumer MUST NOT apply a schedule bound to another tuple, nor substitute another tuple.   deps: ISA-9.2-P3.S10 (closure hash), ISA-11, ISA-12
  <1>5 [req] In `params_hash` a token argument is encoded as its tuple `[B,heap,stack,depth]`.
  <1>6 [req] A budget is classical and fixed before region entry (§3.1), so `budget.mint` is not a region instruction (§5.1).   deps: ISA-3.1, ISA-5.1
  <1>7 [req] (code block, 6 lines) 0 FAULT_NONE 4 FAULT_UB_TRAP 8 FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED
ISA-5.4-P4
  <1>1 [unc] F ≥ 4.
  <1>2 [req] Code 10 is recorded by the R `entropy` device (§7.3) and is also the code a lifted oracle that virtualises entropy uses (`fault 10`) when its entropy input is exhausted.   deps: ISA-2-P3.S1 (lifted oracle), ISA-7.3
ISA-5.4-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Effective cause.** The literal C of `fault C` (in every tier, §4.2, §4.9) and of `lift.faultif p C` records the cause C′ = C if C ≠ 0 and C′ = `FAULT_UB_TRAP` (4) if C = 0; every other row's code is a fixed nonzero constant.   deps: ISA-0.1-P15.S1 (Effective cause), ISA-4.2, ISA-4.9
  <1>2 [req] So no fault is ever recorded as `FAULT_NONE`: a faulted outcome F_B(x) = (0, code) has code ≠ 0, and the fault register distinguishes it from every success (F ≥ 4 makes 4 representable).
  <1>3 [req] Forward and inverse fault writes use C′.
````

### §5.5 Nesting and matched cleanup   [ISA-5.5]

````text
ISA-5.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] A `lift.oracle_call` supplies a caller location `fr'`, clean when computing a fresh outcome.
  <1>2 [req] No automatic propagation: the dialect emits `p = lift.icmp.ne fr' zero; lift.faultif p FAULT_CALLEE` (with `zero` a `lift.const` location) where the source requires it.
  <1>3 [req] To clear `fr'`, the producer emits `lift.oracle_uncall @o` with the same token, callee, `ins` and `args` and `mem` values (no intervening row writes those locations, suite F, nor those cells, below) and the successor versions of `tgt` and `fr'`; the pair shares a dynamic invocation identity.
  <1>4 [req] Alternatively `fr'` is retained until the prefix reversal.   deps: ISA-5.2-P3.S1 (prefix reversal)
  <1>5 [def] Matching is **LIFO**: on every path, a `lift.oracle_uncall` matches the most recent preceding unmatched `lift.oracle_call` with the same callee, token, `ins`, `args` and `mem` operands (two calls followed by two uncalls form two nested pairs); an uncall that matches no call on some path, or different calls on different paths, is ill-formed.   deps: ISA-6.2-P1.S5 (ill-formed)
  <1>6 [req] In an lproc the match includes the fixed bindings of its instance (§3.7); parameter forwarding does not weaken any matching or cleanup condition.   deps: ISA-2-P4.S1 (lproc), ISA-3.7
  <1>7 [req] Suite F rejects a pair when a row on a path between them writes one of its `ins` locations; an intervening `lift.store` is not ill-formed (its address is data): `lift.oracle_uncall` is the same permutation as the call (§4.2), so a pair whose cells changed in between still executes and is undone by the prefix reversal, and clearing `fr'` is then the producer's obligation.   deps: ISA-6.2-P1.S5 (ill-formed), ISA-5.2-P3.S1 (prefix reversal), ISA-4.2
````

### §5.6 Borrowed systems and borrow frames   [ISA-5.6]

````text
ISA-5.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] **Requirement.** A region's completed operation equals its declared operation ⊗ identity on every borrowed bundle and on any external system entangled with it.   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle)
ISA-5.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Rule (suite F).** Borrowed wires (set B) are touched (as control or target) only inside **borrow frames**: maximal contiguous permutation- only subcircuits from the first to the last instruction touching B.
  <1>2 [req] The frame's realised permutation P_F on its wires MUST factor as `P_F = P' ⊗ I_B`, established by a T3 claim over the frame's full domain (exhaustive, or a library certificate, §12 `borrow_frames`) or **structurally by the translation lemma**: the frame is `V; W; V⁻¹; W` where   deps: ISA-14.3-P3.S1 (T3), ISA-12
ISA-5.6-P3
  <1>1 [req] (i) every gate of V is an X-family flip (`x cx ccx mcx`) whose **target is in B** and whose **controls are all in a set X with X ∩ B = ∅**; V touches no other wire; hence V maps b ↦ b ⊕ v(X);
ISA-5.6-P4
  <1>1 [req] (ii) every gate of W is an X-family flip whose **target is outside X, outside B, and outside the set of all controls of W** (as sets, over the whole of W), and W writes no wire of X;
ISA-5.6-P5
  <1>1 [req] (iii) every gate of W has **at most one control in B**;
ISA-5.6-P6
  <1>1 [req] (iv) V⁻¹ is the exact reverse sequence of V; no `swap` appears in the frame.
ISA-5.6-P7
  <1>1 [req] Then W's effect is affine in b, the net map is t ⊕= Σ_g c_g(Y)·v_{j(g)}(X), independent of b, and b is restored (the dirty-ancilla MCX pattern).
  <1>2 [req] Suite F contains the negative tests `cx b y; cx y z; cx b y` (V;W;V⁻¹), `V = cx b2 b1, W = cx b1 t` (b2 ∈ B, violates X ∩ B = ∅), `V = cx b x` (target outside B), and `W = swap y z; cx b y` (swap excluded).
  <1>3 [req] Oracles are one frame verified by their own T3 claim over D.   deps: ISA-14.3-P3.S1 (T3)
ISA-5.6-P8
  <1>1 [req] For (i)–(iii), every gate's controls include its effective control context, and V⁻¹ runs under the same effective control set and wire versions as V.   declared: ISA-2-P10, ISA-3.5, ISA-5.3-P5
  <1>2 [req] Maximality of a frame inside a `qloop` or `qif` body is judged within that body's static instruction sequence, separately for each borrowed lifetime, not across unrolled visits or across distinct arm sequences.   declared: ISA-4.3-P2, ISA-4.3-P4, ISA-4.6, ISA-5.6-P2
````

### §5.7 Executor transformations   [ISA-5.7]

````text
ISA-5.7-P1
  <1>1 [req] Inlining, structure recovery, dispatch re-indexing and simplification MUST produce on every x ∈ D the same final interface tuple as §5.2's construction on the reference body (T6).   deps: ISA-14.3-P6.S1 (T6), ISA-4.2-P29.S1 (reference body), ISA-5.2
  <1>2 [req] Checkpointed and pebbled realisations: §17 item 18.   deps: ISA-17-P19
````

### §6.1 Provenance and transfer   [ISA-6.1]

````text
ISA-6.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] Every workspace bundle version, location version and cell version has provenance `perm` (computed by permutation gates from its **dependency set** S of versions) or `other`.   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle)
  <1>2 [req] Cell versions `(region, i, v)` advance on every write.
  <1>3 [req] Π is the effective control context at the instruction.
ISA-6.1-P2
  <1>1 [req] `qalloc` | perm, S = ∅
ISA-6.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] `d = qcopy s` | d: perm, S = {s} ∪ Π
ISA-6.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] `d = qload r a` | d: perm, S = {a} ∪ cells(r) ∪ Π
ISA-6.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] `qxor s t` | t: perm with S_t ∪ S_s ∪ Π if both perm, else other
ISA-6.1-P6
  <1>1 [req] `qexch a b` | each output: perm with S_a ∪ S_b ∪ Π if both perm, else other
ISA-6.1-P7
  <1>1 [req] `qstore r a v` | each cell (r,i): version advances; perm with S_cell ∪ S_v ∪ {a} ∪ Π if both perm, else other
ISA-6.1-P8
  <1>1 [req] `qexchm r a v` | v and every cell: perm with S_v ∪ ⋃S_cells ∪ {a} ∪ Π if all perm, else other; cell versions advance
ISA-6.1-P9
  <1>1 [req] permutation gate, controls C, target t | t: perm with S_t ∪ C ∪ ⋃S_c ∪ Π iff t was perm, else other
ISA-6.1-P10
  <1>1 [req] diagonal gate on u | unchanged
ISA-6.1-P11
  <1>1 [req] non-diagonal gate on u | u: other; closes the window of every value whose S contains u
ISA-6.1-P12
  <1>1 [req] `oracle_call @o (ins) tgt fr (mem)` | tgt, fr: perm with S = ins ∪ {tgt, fr} ∪ cells(every region passed) ∪ Π; `in` regions unchanged
ISA-6.1-P13
  <1>1 [req] `lift.perm_call` / permutation `action_call` | each mut: perm with S = mut ∪ ins ∪ cells(regions passed) ∪ Π; `mut`-region cells advance with the same S
ISA-6.1-P14
  <1>1 [req] non-permutation `action_call` | every mut and every `mut`-region cell: other
ISA-6.1-P15
  <1>1 [req] `qinplace @g @ginv tk x (ins) (mem) (args)` | x: perm with S_x ∪ ins ∪ cells(every region in `mem`) ∪ Π if x was perm, else other; the `ins` wires and `mem` cells are unchanged
ISA-6.1-P16
  <1>1 [req] lifted rows | each written location/cell: perm with the union of its read operands' sets ∪ Π; written cells' versions advance
ISA-6.1-P17
  <1>1 [req] `qregion` creation | every cell: version 0, perm, S = ∅, with the declared image as its initial value.   declared: ISA-4.6-P1
ISA-6.1-P18
  <1>1 [req] **Outstanding dependence** (for `other` cleanup) extends the dependency test beyond workspace provenance sets to the joint state of all other live values, including interface `mut` wires, region cells, borrowed wires and outstanding diagonal phases.   declared: ISA-3.3-P3, ISA-5.1, ISA-5.3-P1, ISA-6.1-P1
  <1>2 [req] For a candidate inverse of the computing sequence C of g, let G be g's wires and M the composed intervening operation after C and before that inverse, retaining every intervening gate and its effective controls, with internal clean and borrowed lifetimes interpreted as in §14.2.   deps: ISA-14.2   declared: ISA-2-P10, ISA-3.5, ISA-4, ISA-14.2
  <1>3 [req] The remaining values or phases **depend on g** iff there is no single operator V on the remaining wires such that M = I_G ⊗ V for every state of G and every input in the remaining wires' declared domain, including arbitrary external entanglement and the exact global phase.   declared: ISA-5.2-P4, ISA-5.3-P1, ISA-5.6-P1, ISA-14.2
  <1>4 [req] This is a joint, transitive test on the composed operation: cleaning or releasing an intermediate value does not erase its already-transferred dependence, and a diagonal use remains an outstanding phase unless its inverse cancels it in M.   declared: ISA-4.4, ISA-6.3, ISA-14.2
  <1>5 [req] Dependency-set propagation through reads supplies such transitive paths, but absence of a direct provenance edge to g alone does not establish the required factorisation.   declared: ISA-6.1-P1, ISA-14.2
````

### §6.2 Window and obligations   [ISA-6.2]

````text
ISA-6.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] A perm value g with set S is **in its window** from its computation until the first of: a non-diagonal gate on a wire in S or in g; a version advance of a cell in S; a non-permutation action call touching a wire in S; a permutation change to a wire in S not undone before g's cleanup.
  <1>2 [req] A permutation change to a wire of S is **undone** when it and its undoing form a matched pair (§5.3), and every intervening operation leaves the computational-basis values of S and g unchanged; a cell version advance still closes the window even if its value is restored.   deps: ISA-5.3-P7.S1 (matched pair), ISA-5.3   declared: ISA-5.3, ISA-6.1-P1, ISA-14.2
  <1>3 [req] Each cleanup is bound to its exact computing sequence and requires the external input versions that sequence read (the versions in S for a perm value), and the version of g it produced, to be current; g's pre-computation target versions are not required to be current.   declared: ISA-3.3-P3, ISA-6.1-P1
  <1>4 [req] A cleanup runs under the same effective control set, at the same wire versions, as its computing sequence.   declared: ISA-2-P10, ISA-3.5, ISA-5.3-P5
  <1>5 [req] Every perm value MUST be cleaned within its window and before its region exits; otherwise the region is **ill-formed** (closed-window measurement-based cleanup is not admitted).
  <1>6 [req] `other` values are released only by the adjoint of their computing sequence, and only while no other live value, interface wire or outstanding diagonal phase depends on them, as defined in §6.1.   deps: ISA-6.1   declared: ISA-5.3, ISA-6.1, ISA-6.4
````

### §6.3 T5   [ISA-6.3]

````text
ISA-6.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] Cleaning g within its window returns g's wires to |0⟩ and factorises them from the remaining state; diagonal uses of g or of its dependencies have applied the corresponding diagonal phases to the remainder, which is part of the program's declared semantics.
````

### §6.4 Effective control and cleanup realisations   [ISA-6.4]

````text
ISA-6.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] Every cleanup in this version is **unitary**: realisation `reverse` (the adjoint of g's exact computing sequence, §6.2) or `recompute` (legal for `perm` values only: recompute g into a fresh clean bundle by the same sequence, `qxor` it into g's wires, uncompute the fresh bundle by the adjoint).   deps: ISA-2-P1.S2 (bundle), ISA-6.2
  <1>2 [req] **Measurement-based cleanup is not admitted in sched/ cert 0.9**: a schedule naming any other realisation is invalid, the target capability `mbu` is reserved and MUST be `false`, and no cleanup produces a `channel` claim.   deps: ISA-17-P7.S1 (Measurement-based cleanup)
  <1>3 [non] *(non-normative)* The fixup after an X-basis measurement of g with outcome m is the phase (−1)^{m·g(x)}, a function of g's computing sequence and not of the target; its normative form, its controlled variant and its certificate kind are deferred (§17 item 6; default: unitary cleanup).   deps: ISA-17-P7
  <1>4 [req] Schedules and certificate cleanup entries are keyed by `(region hash, variant, inherited control count)`; a region reachable under a non-empty control context MUST have a cleanup schedule for that key.
````

### §7.1 Classical memory (CC, R)   [ISA-7.1]

````text
ISA-7.1-P1
  <1>1 [unc] Byte-addressed, little-endian, sparse.
  <1>2 [req] `layout` partitions the address space: a **null region** `[0, null_size)` never allocated (null_size ≥ 1); globals at fixed bases with images; the heap `[heap_base, heap_base + heap_limit_max)`, all disjoint, `heap_base + heap_limit_max ≤ 2^ptr_ width`, and the number of globals ≤ 2^A_tab, all validated at load.
  <1>3 [req] `p = alloc n` **fails before any mutation** when bump + max(n, 1) > heap_base + heap_limit_max or the table holds 2^A_tab entries (CC trap / R fault `FAULT_BUDGET_HEAP`); otherwise it returns the bump pointer, records `(base, size = n, live = 1, pinned = 0)` and advances by `max(n, 1)`; globals have pre-entered pinned live entries; an access is valid iff its whole byte range lies in one live entry; `free p` marks the unique live unpinned entry with base p dead (unpinned entries are heap entries, whose bases strictly increase; pinned entries cannot be freed and a pinned entry with base p is left unchanged; no live unpinned entry with base p: CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_MEMFAULT`); storage is never reclaimed.   deps: ISA-4.9-P1.S1 (CC trap)
  <1>4 [req] Initial state: bump = `heap_base`, table = the pre-entries in layout order, memory zero except images.
````

### §7.2 Lifted memory of an oracle   [ISA-7.2]

````text
ISA-7.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] `mem` has 2^H byte cells (H ≤ ptr_width); `alloctab` 2^A_tab entries `(base, size, live, pinned)`; the stack 2^S_cells cells.
  <1>2 [req] The `layout` fixes `null_size`, each global's base and image, `heap_base`, `heap_ limit_max`, and for each **interface region** of the oracle (W = 8 required) a base address; all ranges disjoint and within `[0, 2^H)`, and for every oracle the number of pre-entries (globals plus its interface regions) ≤ 2^A_tab, checked at load.
  <1>3 [req] `lift.load`/`lift.store` dispatch by address range to `mem` or to the mapped interface region (role `in` preserved by the construction).   deps: ISA-7.2-P1.S2 (interface region)
  <1>4 [req] The low H bits address cells; `inrange` guarantees the range lies in a live entry, hence within `[0, 2^H)`.
ISA-7.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Memoryless objects.** An object without a `layout` section MUST contain no lprocs, no `lift.addr lift.boundscheck lift.load lift.store lift.alloc lift.free lift.call lift.ret` rows, no `mem` interface slots and no CC/R `alloc free load store`; H = A_tab = S_cells = 0, no `mem`, `alloctab`, stack or counters are allocated, and `bennett_budget` requires `heap_limit = stack_limit = depth_limit = 0` (§5.4).   deps: ISA-2-P4.S1 (lproc), ISA-5.4
  <1>2 [ex] Example 1 of §16.3 is memoryless.   deps: ISA-16.3-P2.S1 (Example 1), ISA-16.3
````

### §7.3 Device models and tapes (R)   [ISA-7.3]

````text
ISA-7.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] Every device operation takes classical-memory operands and writes its results to memory; each `effect` is **atomic**: validated (operands in range, tape available) before any change, and a failing validation is a fault record with no partial delta.
ISA-7.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] `console` | byte sequence (empty) | `write(ptr, len)` | – | `len`; pop
ISA-7.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] `clock` | `c: u64` (0) | `read(ptr)`: writes c (8 bytes LE) at ptr, then c += 1 | – | overwritten 8 bytes; c −= 1
ISA-7.3-P4
  <1>1 [req] `entropy` | position `p` (0) into the entropy tape (§10) | `read(ptr, len)`: copies tape[p..p+len) to ptr; p += len | p + len > length: fault `FAULT_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED` | overwritten bytes; p −= len   deps: ISA-10
ISA-7.3-P5
  <1>1 [req] `block` | sector map from the `block_image` (else empty), 512-byte sectors; absent sectors read as zero | `read(sector, ptr)`; `write(sector, ptr)` | – | read: overwritten 512 bytes; write: the old sector contents **and a presence bit** (absent sectors are removed again on reversal)
ISA-7.3-P6
  <1>1 [req] **BLOCK-IMAGE** (K10; source: bennett-vm-47i). `layout.block_image` names a data symbol (§9.1, §16.1).   deps: ISA-0.2-P10.S1 (K10), ISA-9.1, ISA-16.1
  <1>2 [req] Decode each successive pair of its lowercase hex digits to one byte, in textual order.
  <1>3 [req] Its decoded length L MUST be a multiple of 512, including L = 0.
  <1>4 [req] At block-device initialisation, before executing any instruction or changing device state, reject an image of any other length; never pad or truncate it.
  <1>5 [req] For 0 ≤ s < L/512, sector number s is present and its byte at offset b (0 ≤ b < 512) is image[512s + b].
  <1>6 [req] There is no sector header, length prefix, sector-number field or reversal of bytes within a sector.
  <1>7 [req] An all-zero sector in the image is present.
  <1>8 [req] Every other sector is absent and reads as 512 zero bytes; no image and an empty image give an empty map.
  <1>9 [req] This specifies the initial map only; the §7.3 write/reversal presence-bit rule remains in force.   deps: ISA-7.3
  <1>10 [req] Motivation (0.8 §7.3): "sector map from the `block_image` (else empty), 512-byte sectors; absent sectors read as zero"; §9.1: "`data` lines are `NAME SP HEX`".   deps: ISA-9.1
  <1>11 [req] The contiguous encoding and partial-sector policy are additions, not a claimed 0.8 loader requirement.
ISA-7.3-P7
  <1>1 [unc] **BLOCK-IMAGE witness**   deps: ISA-7.3-P6.S1 (BLOCK-IMAGE)
  <1>2 [ex] (code block, 3 lines) {"length":1024,"present_sectors":[0,1],"sector_first_bytes":[[0,0],[1,255]],"abs…
ISA-7.3-P8
  <1>1 [req] The image is 512 bytes 00 followed by 512 bytes ff (2048 hex digits).
  <1>2 [req] Sector 0 is present although zero; sector 1 is ff throughout; sector 2 is absent and reads zero.
  <1>3 [req] Writing sector 2 then reversing removes it; writing sector 0 then reversing restores a present zero sector.
ISA-7.3-P9
  <1>1 [req] Each `effect` appends `(dev, op, args)` to the effect tape.
````

### §7.4 Run history and the dynamic SSA model (CC, R)   [ISA-7.4]

````text
ISA-7.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] The classical environment holds **dynamic instances**: every executed defining instruction creates a new instance retained in the run history until reversal; a name denotes its most recent instance.
  <1>2 [req] Frames:   deps: ISA-2-P6.S1 (Frame)
ISA-7.4-P2
  <1>1 [req] any defining instruction | its defined instance
ISA-7.4-P3
  <1>1 [req] `br` | predecessor block, prior block-parameter instances
ISA-7.4-P4
  <1>1 [req] `store` | address, width, overwritten bytes
ISA-7.4-P5
  <1>1 [req] `alloc` | old bump pointer, the table entry written, the zero-filled range
ISA-7.4-P6
  <1>1 [req] `free` | the entry's old live bit
ISA-7.4-P7
  <1>1 [req] `call` | invocation boundary (callee, argument values)
ISA-7.4-P8
  <1>1 [req] `ret` | result values, the callee's activation and the frame link
ISA-7.4-P9
  <1>1 [req] `uncall` | the reversed segment's id (skipped by whole-run reversal, below)
ISA-7.4-P10
  <1>1 [req] `effect` | tape index plus the device-specific record of §7.3; reversal also removes its effect-tape entry   deps: ISA-7.3
ISA-7.4-P11
  <1>1 [req] `hostcall` | payload bytes and reply bytes
ISA-7.4-P12
  <1>1 [req] `qreg.*`, `measure` | the ledger record of §3.3 (ids, class, widths, prior states, whether a free's cleanliness was verified) and the measured bits   deps: ISA-3.3
ISA-7.4-P13
  <1>1 [req] `budget.mint` | the token and its tuple; reversal revokes the token
ISA-7.4-P14
  <1>1 [req] `oracle_call` / `action_call` | (region hash, variant, inherited control count, classical args with every token's tuple, register ids): reversed by re-application / adjoint, exactly once, by this frame
ISA-7.4-P15
  <1>1 [req] fault record (a failing instruction, `trap`, `fault`) | cause code (§4.9) and program point; terminal.   deps: ISA-4.9
  <1>2 [req] Reversal (§10) removes the record; the failing instruction had no other effect, so the state is then the state before it   deps: ISA-10
ISA-7.4-P16
  <1>1 [unc] **Logical history.** Frames and dynamic instances specify the *logical* history.   deps: ISA-2-P6.S1 (Frame), ISA-7.4-P1.S1 (dynamic instances)
  <1>2 [req] An executor MAY store it by checkpoints, deltas or deterministic replay, provided it reconstructs the same logical frames, instances, reversal marks and traversal order; it never re-issues an external event (effects are replayed from the effect tape and host replies from their frames, never requested again), never re-executes a region call to recover its record, and never copies quantum state.
  <1>3 [req] T4 is stated over the logical history.   deps: ISA-14.3-P4.S1 (T4)
  <1>4 [req] **Active and audit history.** The *active* history is the sequence of frames not marked reversed; reversed frames and `uncall` markers remain as immutable *audit records*.
  <1>5 [req] Undoing a defining frame removes its dynamic instance from the active environment although its audit record is retained.
ISA-7.4-P17
  <1>1 [req] **Pure frames.** A frame is **pure** iff it belongs to `br` or to a defining instruction among `const`, the binops, `udiv..srem`, `icmp`, `select`, `zext sext trunc`, `ptrtoint inttoptr`, `load`, `qreg.width qreg.id qreg.from_id`: it changes only the set of instances.
  <1>2 [req] Every other frame (`store alloc free call ret uncall trap fault effect hostcall qreg.new qreg.free qreg.slice qreg.concat measure budget.mint`, region calls, fault records) is impure.
ISA-7.4-P18
  <1>1 [req] **History traversal** (the one reversal procedure, used by segment `uncall` and by whole-run reversal). A range of frames is **reversed** by visiting its frames in LIFO order; a frame already marked reversed and an `uncall` frame are **skipped**; every other frame is undone by its row of the table above and then marked reversed.   deps: ISA-5.5-P1.S5 (LIFO)
  <1>2 [req] Reversed frames stay in the history, marked, and are never undone again.
  <1>3 [req] An `uncall` marker is always skipped: when a later traversal (an enclosing segment's `uncall`, or whole-run reversal) reaches it, the frames of the segment it names are already marked and are skipped too, so neither the marker nor its segment is undone, re-executed or redone a second time.
ISA-7.4-P19
  <1>1 [def] **Segment uncall** (`uncall @f (args) (results)`).
  <1>2 [req] Let S be the most recent completed call segment of the history (a `call` frame, its matching `ret` frame and every frame between them).
  <1>3 [req] The `uncall` is legal iff S is a call of `@f`, S's recorded boundary argument and result values equal the operand values, **every frame after S is pure**, and S contains, at any nesting depth, **no `measure` frame** and no `qreg. free` frame whose cleanliness was not verified (hardware, §17 item 14); otherwise it is a CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP` and changes nothing beyond the fault record (§4.9).   deps: ISA-4.9-P1.S1 (CC trap), ISA-17-P15, ISA-4.9
  <1>4 [req] Execution reverses S by the history traversal (nested segments are undone; nested segments already cancelled by an inner `uncall`, and that inner `uncall` frame, are skipped), and pushes an `uncall` frame naming S.
  <1>5 [req] The instances defined inside S no longer exist; using such a name before it is redefined is a CC trap / R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP`.   deps: ISA-4.9-P1.S1 (CC trap)
  <1>6 [def] **Whole-run reversal** (§10) is the history traversal over the whole history: S's effects on memory, the allocation table, devices, the register ledger and tokens were undone by the `uncall`, and the frames between S and the `uncall` are pure, so at the `uncall` frame every component except the retained instances already equals its value before S.   deps: ISA-3.3-P7.S1 (register ledger), ISA-10
  <1>7 [req] T4 is stated over these frames.   deps: ISA-14.3-P4.S1 (T4)
  <1>8 [non] *(non-normative)* S is never re-executed and never redone; the compute–copy–`uncall` idiom derives what it keeps through pure instructions before the `uncall`.
````

### §8.2 Resources, aggregation, timing   [ISA-8.2]

````text
ISA-8.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] (code block, 3 lines) "resources": { "<name>": { "kind": "count"|"time"|"occupancy"|"peak", "unit": "<…
ISA-8.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] Mandatory: `qubit_second` (occupancy, per class), `time`, `peak_qubits` (peak, per class).
  <1>2 [req] Aggregation from the **scheduled event list** (every **leaf event** — a native gate after scheme expansion, a classical step, an effect — with its start time and duration, every wire with its live interval): `count` sums the per-event costs, each leaf exactly once (a scheme contributes only its expanded template, never a cost of its own); `time` is the makespan; `occupancy` integrates, per class, the number of live wires times the class rate over time (a class absent from `rate` has rate 1); `peak` is the maximum over time of the number of concurrently live wires per class (concurrent demands sum).
  <1>3 [req] Classical instructions and effects take `classical_step_time`.
  <1>4 [req] Sequential in program order unless the schedule assigns start times; a gate occupies its wires for its `time`; gates on disjoint wires MAY overlap unless `max_parallel` is declared.
  <1>5 [req] Connectivity is all-to-all when `topology` is absent, and is constrained by §8.3 when present (§17 item 15).   deps: ISA-8.3, ISA-17-P16
  <1>6 [req] Interface wires are charged to the caller for the call's duration; borrowed wires to the borrower at `dirty_rate`, replacing the owner's charge.
````

````text
  <1>1 [req] **Model.** A run executes a device CC entry; the host passes classical arguments, register ids and the entropy tape, receives classical results, fault codes and declared measurements; host services are reached by `hostcall`.
  <1>2 [def] **Positional binding**: argument i of `bennett_ run` binds to parameter i of the entry's signature: `INT(width, bytes)` to `iN` with width = N (else `E_ARG`), `F64` to `f64`, `QREG` to `qreg[n]` with the register's n or to `qreg[*]` with any width, `TOKEN` to `token` (a valid token, §5.4).   deps: ISA-5.4
  <1>3 [req] Arguments and the entropy tape are **copied** at `bennett_run`; the caller may free its buffers afterwards.
  <1>4 [req] Host-minted tokens are scoped to the program and destroyed at unload; device-minted tokens to their run (§5.4).   deps: ISA-5.4
  <1>5 [req] Accessor-returned pointers are valid until the owning object is freed.
  <1>6 [req] `bennett_unload` with a run not CLOSED: `E_INVALID_STATE`.
ISA-10-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Invocation tree.** A run record is a tree (CC segments, R calls, Q calls); an R call's subtree is owned by its R history; `bennett_reverse` reverses post-order: CC segments by their run history, R calls by LIFO reversal of their history (§7.4, reversed segments and `uncall` frames skipped), top-level Q calls by re-application / adjoint.   deps: ISA-5.5-P1.S5 (LIFO), ISA-7.4
  <1>2 [req] A fault record is terminal (§4.9): the run is `FAILED`, and every activation open at the fault keeps its frames, which reversal undoes like those of a call that returned.   deps: ISA-4.9
ISA-10-P3
  <1>1 [req] **States.** `CREATED → RUNNING → (SUSPENDED ⇄ RUNNING) → (HOST_REQUEST ⇄ RUNNING) → COMPLETED | FAILED`; `COMPLETED → REVERSED`; `FAILED → REVERSED`; any of `COMPLETED/FAILED/REVERSED → CLOSED` (`bennett_run_close` releases the record; register ids created by the run remain valid unless measured or freed).
  <1>2 [req] A run owns the registers and memory it touches exclusively while not CLOSED; a register reached by `qreg.from_id` is touched from then on; `bennett_qreg_prepare`, `bennett_qreg_free` and a `bennett_run` argument naming a register owned by another run that is not CLOSED are `E_INVALID_STATE`.
  <1>3 [req] **Reverse eligibility**: `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`; no `measure` frame; no `qreg.free` frame whose cleanliness was not verified (§17 item 14); no register it touched has been prepared, freed, sliced or used by another run since; else `E_NOT_REVERSIBLE`.   deps: ISA-17-P15
  <1>4 [req] Reversing a `FAILED` run first undoes its terminal fault record, then traverses the rest of its history exactly as for a completed run, including the frames of activations that never returned; the run is then `REVERSED` with every component T4 names at its entry value.   deps: ISA-14.3-P4.S1 (T4), ISA-4.9-P1.S2 (terminal fault record)
  <1>5 [req] `bennett_qreg_prepare` and `bennett_ qreg_free` require a clean register (`E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN` otherwise on a verifying executor; a non-verifying one: §17 item 14); there is no reset and no trace-out: a register in unknown state is released by a `measure` inside a run, which consumes its handle (§3.3).   deps: ISA-2-P9.S1 (non-verifying), ISA-17-P15, ISA-3.3
ISA-10-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Results.** `bennett_result_get` writes value i and sets `*kind` and `*width`: `INT` as ⌈N/8⌉ little-endian bytes, `*width` = N; `F64` as the 8 IEEE 754 binary64 little-endian bytes, `*width` = 64; `QREG` and `TOKEN` as the 8-byte little-endian id, `*width` = 64.
  <1>2 [req] A `cap` smaller than that byte count is `E_ARG` and nothing is written.
  <1>3 [req] Fault records are read by `bennett_result_nfaults` / `bennett_result_fault` (codes of §4.9; a `COMPLETED` run has none, a `FAILED` run has exactly one, its terminal record, and exposes no values).   deps: ISA-4.9
  <1>4 [req] For an R `fault C`, `bennett_wait` returns `OK` with `*result_out` set and `*request_out` NULL as for any `FAILED` run; `bennett_result_nvalues` is 0, `bennett_result_nfaults` is 1 and `bennett_result_fault(result, 0)` is exactly C when C ≠ 0 (4 when C = 0, §5.4), with all 64 bits preserved.   deps: ISA-5.4
  <1>5 [req] The fault code is result data, not a `bennett_status` error or a host-service reply.
ISA-10-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Waiting.** `bennett_wait` blocks until the run leaves `RUNNING` and returns `OK` with exactly one outcome: `HOST_REQUEST` (`*request_out` set, `*result_out` NULL; `bennett_reply` answers it and the run is `RUNNING` again) or `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` (`*result_out` set, `*request_ out` NULL).
  <1>2 [req] Waiting on a `SUSPENDED`, `REVERSED` or `CLOSED` run is `E_ INVALID_STATE`.
ISA-10-P6
  <1>1 [req] **`hostcall`.** `rlen = hostcall service ptr len`: `[ptr, ptr + len)` MUST lie in one live allocation (else CC trap and no request is made); those bytes are copied into the request; the run enters `HOST_REQUEST`; the reply payload is written to `[ptr, ptr + min(len, reply length))` and `rlen` = the full reply length (so truncation is detectable; a reply whose length does not fit `ptr_width` bits is refused by `bennett_reply` with `E_ARG` before any write, and the run stays in `HOST_REQUEST`); the frame records the request bytes, the overwritten bytes and the reply bytes.   deps: ISA-4.9-P1.S1 (CC trap)
  <1>2 [req] Every `service` is declared in `devices.services`; an undeclared one is a load error.
ISA-10-P7
  <1>1 [req] **Tape.** `bennett_tape_next` yields each `effect` in tape order; `args` holds the operation's operands in the order of §7.3, each an unsigned 64-bit little-endian field (pointers zero-extended from `ptr_width`), so `*alen` = 8 × arity.   deps: ISA-7.3
````

````text
ISA-10.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Resource rows.** `estimate_nresources` counts scalar rows, not target resource declarations.

  <1>3 [req] Each `occupancy` or `peak` resource has one row **for every target class**, including unused classes with value zero, named `escape(resource)[escape(class)]`; no sum across classes is substituted.
  <1>4 [req] `escape` percent-encodes the UTF-8 bytes except ASCII letters, digits, `-._~`, using uppercase hex (including `%`, `[` and `]`).

ISA-10.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Decimal values.** Aggregation is exact rational arithmetic; rounding occurs only at the accessor boundary.
  <1>2 [req] `value_decimal` is the least nonnegative decimal with at most **34 significant digits** that is ≥ the exact resource value.
  <1>3 [req] For q > 0 let e be the unique integer with 10^e ≤ q < 10^(e+1); return `ceil(q / 10^(e−33)) × 10^(e−33)`.
  <1>4 [req] Zero is `0`.

  <1>6 [req] Exact integers and terminating rationals that fit are unchanged.

ISA-10.1-P6
````
